title: I'm not convinced the AI bubble exists
lede: Matteo Raso argues the AI boom may not be a bubble: data-centre spending is mostly one-off, Anthropic's S-1 shows strong unit economics, and the big public AI companies trade at ordinary earnings multiples.

points: The post puts industry spending and commitments near 5 trillion dollars and treats most of it as one-time data-centre build-out.
It cites Anthropic's S-1 as earning $2.08 per $1 of compute, with revenue reaching 16.3 billion dollars in the first half of 2026.
Alphabet, Meta and NVIDIA have price-to-earnings ratios in their 20s, unlike the loss-making firms of the dot-com bubble.
It argues brand loyalty and enterprise contracts can keep AI labs profitable without a lasting technical moat.

points.text: Commenters reject treating data centres as one-off costs, since GPUs age quickly and keep needing replacement.
One points out the post mixes up Alphabet's revenue with its earnings when estimating how debt could be repaid.
Several say the post discusses revenue while claiming profits, and that price wars may let customers capture the margin.
Many accept the technology is useful but compare the risk to railroads and dot-com: a timing bubble, not a dead end.
